question: On synth-1m, what is the total log return of the instrument over the whole sample? Report it as the statistic `total_log_return`, and test the hypothesis that the mean session log return differs from zero (two-sided, 5% level).

plan.hypothesis: The mean session log return of the roll-adjusted SYN front-month future on synth-1m differs from zero.
plan.method: Load synth-1m (symbol SYN). Convert ts from UTC to America/New_York and assign each bar to a trading session: the session runs 18:00 to 17:00 New York time, and a bar at or after 18:00 belongs to the next calendar day's session date. Keep sessions dated 2023-01-02 to 2025-12-31. Sort by ts and compute 1-minute log returns ln(close_t / close_{t-1}) only between consecutive bars of the same contract; the return across each of the 12 contract switches (a roll, not a price move) is dropped, so the series is roll-adjusted. Also drop the return across each session break (17:00 to 18:00) only if the two bars belong to different contracts; otherwise keep it in the session it lands in, so returns sum to the whole-sample move. Session log return = sum of the bar log returns assigned to that session. total_log_return = sum of all session log returns over the sample (equivalently the sum of within-contract bar log returns). Report total_log_return, the number of sessions, the mean and standard deviation of session log returns, and the unadjusted ln(last close / first close) for comparison, which includes the roll gaps.
plan.significance: Two-sided test of mean session log return = 0 at the 5% level: Newey-West HAC t-test on the session log returns with lag 5 (sessions do not overlap; the lag guards against mild serial correlation), with the plain one-sample t-test reported alongside.

summary.text: Over the whole sample (783 sessions, 2023-01-02 to 2025-12-31), the roll-adjusted total log return of SYN on synth-1m is 0.5658. The mean session log return is 0.000723, and it differs from zero at the 5% level: Newey-West HAC t = 5.20 (p ≈ 2.6e-7), plain t = 4.93 (p ≈ 1.0e-6). The hypothesis is supported. Without the roll adjustment, ln(last/first close) is 0.8073; the 12 contract-roll gaps account for the difference of about 0.24.
